description: Figure 8(b) illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing on the Llama2 model, with the y-axis representing accuracy (ACC) in percentage and the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³. The plot compares the performance of five different editing methods: Base (LLM without editing), MEND, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME. The Base method, represented by a black line with circle markers, shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 64% to 71%. The FT method, shown with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at about 65% and rises to 72%. The MEND method, depicted with a brown line and square markers, begins at 70% and increases to 80%. The MEMIT method, represented by a purple line and diamond markers, starts at 69% and reaches 77%. The ROME method, shown with a green line and square markers, starts at 74% and increases to 82%. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
